entities.text: Vittal Kusuma vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against petitioner/Accused No.1 in C.C.No.60 of 2013 on the file of V Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 478, 471, 406, 419, 420 and 120-B of IPC.
2.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Ms.Ayesha Saba, Advocate representing the counsel for petitioner, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1/State and Sri T.S.Praveen Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3. When the matter is taken up, Ms.Ayesha Saba, Advocate appearing on behalf of the counsel for petitioner on record, seeks for adjournment.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has opposed for adjournment contending that seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.1161 of 2008 on the file of VI Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, the petitioner herein has earlier filed another quash petition i.e. Crl.P.No.143 of 2009 and the same was dismissed by this Court by order dated 01.05.2009.

Since the present petition is filed after re-numbering of the same calendar case as C.C.No.60 of 2013 on its GAC, J transfer to the Court of V Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, this quash petition is not maintainable.

entities.text: Court of V Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. On perusal of the counter affidavit, it is evident that initially a private complaint has been filed by respondent No.2 herein against Accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offences under Sections 468, 471, 406,
419, 420, 120-B, 447, 427 and 506 of IPC and the same was referred to the Police under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
It is the specific contention of respondent No.2 that the Police have filed final report without conducting proper investigation.
Being aggrieved by the same, a protest petition was filed by respondent No.2, and basing on it, the Court took cognizance of the case.

There was a clear allegation against accused Nos.2 and 3 that they trespassed into the land of the complainant on the strength of forged and fabricated documents which are alleged to have been executed by accused No.1 and that accused No.1 did not have any right to execute the sale deed.

5. It is a matter of fact to be adjudicated by way of evidence as to whether accused Nos.2 and 3 have trespassed into the land of the complainant and whether accused No.1 has executed the sale deed basing on the forged and fabricated documents.

Moreover, the record shows that the initial quash petition filed for quashing the proceedings in GAC, J C.C.No.1161 of 2008 on the file of VI Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, has been dismissed by this Court on 01.05.2009 after hearing both the parties.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the present quash petition which has been filed to quash the same proceedings in the re-numbered C.C.No.60 of 2013 on its being transferred to the Court of V Metropolitan Magistrate, Medchal, is not maintainable.
